thread.title: Markets Are Down Big as Stocks Give Back Gains From Record-Setting Session - TheStreet

author: Tony Owusu
title: Markets Are Down Big as Stocks Give Back Gains From Record-Setting Session - TheStreet
text:
Dec27,20181:18PMEST Spencer paltt/Getty Three Things to Know Thursday The Dow had its highest single-day point increase in its history on Wednesday, jumping 1,086 points in the post-Christmas session. All three major indices are experiencing sharp declines following Wednesday's rally. Initial jobless claims fell by 1,000 last week to 216,000.
U.S. markets are having trouble sustaining momentum from Wednesday's record breaking session with all three major indices falling sharply shortly after the opening bell Thursday, December 27.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average had the strongest point increase in its history Wednesday, jumping more than 1,000 points on the session after markets had been pummeled leading into the holiday break.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.7%, or 393 points to 22,485, while the S&P 500 fell 1.85% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.33% .
The retail sector was one of the leading sectors from Thursday's rally as the segment basks in the glow of strong holiday season. Sales from November 1 through Christmas Eve were up 5.1% to more than $850 billion, according to Mastercard SpendingPulse. Online sales jumped 19% year over year.
During Wednesday's session, the SPDR S&P Retail ETF ( XRT ) jumped 5.75% thanks to retailers like Kohl's Corp. ( KSS ) , Foot Locker Inc. ( FL ) and American Eagle Outfitters Inc. ( AEO ) having strong sessions.
Foot Locker shares are down 1%, Kohl's shares are falling 3.6%, and American Eagle fell 2.4%.
Tech stocks also had a strong session, with all five FAANG stocks posting increases above 6%. But Thursday's session did not have the same ring to it.
Facebook Inc. ( FB ) shares fell 1.8%, while Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ) shares fell 3.5%, Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) shares declined 3.2%, Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) shares declined 3.3%, and Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) shares dropped 2.7%.
Shares of Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ) were coming back down to earth Thursday after jumping more than 10% Wednesday after Wedbush analyst Daniel Ives reiterated an outperform rating and price target of $440. Tesla shares are down more than 2% Thursday.
U.S. jobless claims fell for the third time in the last four weeks by 1,000 to 216,000 for the week ended December 22, according to the U.S. Department of labor. Economists polled by Reuters were expecting an increase of 217,000.
Oil prices were struggling once again Thursday after also having a strong session Wednesday. Global benchmark Brent crude was down 1.6% to $53.61 per barrel while U.S. benchmark West Texas crude fell 1.25% to $45.64 per barrel.
